results.content: Palliative care teams typically consist of multiple healthcare providers, including physicians, nurses, social workers, chaplains, and other specialists, who work together to address the physical, psychological, social, and spiritual needs of seriously ill patients and their families (8). The delivery of the same health education plan (for a roomful of patients representing different cultures, different insurance plans, a variety of ages, and multiple comorbid medical conditions) is biased because it will most likely cause a disparity in care and treatment. By ensuring that all parties involved in the patient care continuum fully understand the SDoH and their potential negative health outcomes, nursing management members continue to lead efforts to improve healthcare and future health outcomes for society. From patients misunderstanding instructions as they relate to immediate care and post discharge plans of treatment, to the unintentional use of ‘medical jargon” of the part of the medical provider, any gaps in the delivery care model due to extenuating factors, health care and health literacy must be continually assessed to make sure all involved are “on the same page”.
